problem.title: Three reasons your team tools never stick.
problem.p1d: In a shared tool, an intern and a director see the same thing. <hl>The hierarchy only exists in people's heads</hl>, never in the tool.
problem.p2t: The tool doesn't keep up with your needs
problem.p2d: A team splits, a manager leaves. You have to <hl>redo access, spaces and views</hl> instead of getting on with the work.
problem.p3t: No one can see who's doing what
problem.p3d: Without visibility into who's doing what, a project starts <hl>without knowing if it's even feasible</hl>. You find out midway, once it's too late.

pyramid.title: Invite your team.
pyramid.subtitle: Everyone joins with the Cosmo account they already have. You give them a role and teams: <hl>they only see their own scope</hl>, no more, no less.
pyramid.g1d: By email, by code, by link or from your Cosmo contacts. Everyone keeps their account and gets the default role straight away.
pyramid.g2d: You write your roles and tick their permissions. For an assignment, a role can end on its own at a set date.
pyramid.g3d: Teams carry projects, OKRs and statistics. One person can belong to several teams. <hl>A project is only visible to its teams.</hl>
pyramid.roleAria: Example role editor: the Project lead role and its permissions
pyramid.note: Confidential by default, and less noise: everyone opens Cosmo on their own work, not the whole company's.

projects.title: Create your projects, assign them at any scale.
projects.subtitle: Assign, that's it. <hl>The task lands in each assignee's personal Cosmo.</hl>
projects.p1d: One person, several, or <hl>subtasks</hl>, to anyone you want within your scope.
projects.p2d: What to do? The list. When? The timeline. Where do we stand? The portfolio.
projects.p3d: Mention someone in a task: they're notified, and the badge stays until they read it.

execution.title: Track execution.
execution.subtitle: <hl>Statuses, health and dependencies.</hl> You see what moves and what blocks.
execution.p1d: A task's assignees update its health, so a problem gets fixed before it's too late.
execution.p2d: To do, in progress, in review, blocked, done. A review is approved or sent back in one click.
execution.p3d: Link tasks to show what blocks what.
execution.healthAria: A task's Health menu: on track, at risk, off track, achieved
execution.depsAria: Dependency example: three linked tasks, the last one blocked by the one before

okr.title: Set your objectives, at every scale.
okr.subtitle: An organization objective breaks down into team OKRs, each OKR into numeric key results. <hl>Every team sees how its work feeds the shared objective</hl>.
okr.orgExample: Make Nova Studio a reference in independent branding
okr.team1Objective: Make every identity delivered a reference in its industry
okr.team2Objective: Build an acquisition engine that no longer relies on word of mouth
okr.team3Objective: Become the agency clients know they can count on
okr.b1: Every team OKR attaches to the organization objective that gives it meaning.
okr.b2: A key result is a number to hit, not a vague intention.
okr.b3: An objective can be visible to the whole company, to some teams, or only to the people you pick.

progress.title: Track how everyone is progressing.
progress.subtitle: Activity reports answer the Monday morning question: <hl>what moved forward, and thanks to whom</hl>. Readable for the whole company or one team, by day, week or month.
progress.p1t: What moved forward, day after day
progress.p1d: Every night, Cosmo records what the company and each team did: completed tasks, projects and OKRs that progressed, events held.
progress.p2d: The detail per person, tasks completed and events held, so work gets recognized rather than guessed.
progress.p3d: On each team's page, open and overdue tasks for every member. A task is reassigned by drag and drop, before the steering meeting rather than during it.
progress.overviewBody: The home screen of the company space: what's waiting for you (tasks to approve, mentions, people you're blocking), your workload for the week, your calendar and your key results. You approve without leaving the screen. That is where <hl>the day starts</hl>.

more.title: A few more features.
more.subtitle: What other tools are missing, <hl>and what your team will actually use</hl>.
more.f1d: Pick the team, Cosmo suggests the slots where everyone is free.
more.f2d: One email a day with what you haven't read. Everything else is set type by type.
more.f3d: Ctrl K searches projects, tasks, goals and people. Only what you're allowed to see.
more.f4t: Reminders go out on their own
more.f4d: A task runs late or changes status, and Cosmo tells the right person.
more.f5d: Select, assign, complete. No more one click at a time.
more.f6d: Every task change lands in your channel.
more.f7d: Before removing someone, an assistant hands over their tasks and goals. Nothing is left orphaned.
more.f8d: Their role ends on its own on the set day.
more.f9d: Verify your domain, and only your addresses can join.
more.f10t: The conversation stays in the project
more.f10d: One thread per project. Newcomers read the history instead of asking.
more.f11d: 30 days in the trash, history included.
more.f12d: Members, teams, permissions: everything is logged for a year.
more.f13d: Export everything to CSV, any time.

security.title: The questions your committee will ask.
security.subtitle: We answer them here, <hl>before they block the rollout</hl>.
security.s1d: Access rules <hl>live in the database, not in the code shown on screen</hl>. No one can bypass them by tampering with a request.
security.s2d: A manager sees the team projects and tasks in their scope. A member's habits, calendar and personal tasks <hl>stay invisible to their management chain</hl>.
security.s3d: No data is ever resold. <hl>Account deletion is real, not symbolic</hl>, and every retention period is written down.
security.s4t: Leaving is as easy as joining
security.s4d: Ownership transfer, a member's departure with their work handed over, deleting the organization: it all takes a few clicks, <hl>no support ticket needed</hl>.

faq.title: Organization questions
faq.q1: Do my teammates need to create a new account?
faq.a1: No. A member joins your organization with the Cosmo account they already have, by email, code or invitation link. Their personal space stays separate and belongs to them.
faq.q2: Can a manager see their team's personal tasks?
faq.a2: No. The management scope covers team work: projects, assigned tasks, OKRs, collective statistics. A member's personal tasks, habits and calendar are never exposed to their management chain.
faq.q3: Can two teams work without seeing each other?
faq.a3: Yes, that's the default. A project is only visible to its teams, and the rule is enforced in the database, not merely hidden in the interface.
faq.q4: What happens if we go past a tier?
faq.a4: You can't invite past your tier until you raise it. But no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down afterwards.
faq.q5: Can we try without committing the company?
faq.a4Free: Nothing blocks you today: during the launch offer every tier is free and you can invite as many people as you want. Once billing is switched on, you will no longer be able to invite past your tier until you raise it. But no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down.
faq.a5: Yes. Create an organization of up to five members, free and without a credit card. It is the complete product, not a crippled version.
faq.a5Free: Yes. Create your organization free and without a credit card, whatever your headcount, for as long as the launch offer runs. It is the complete product, not a crippled version.
